description.main: Catalogue of the Whitney Museum's 2026–27 retrospective Roy Lichtenstein: Like New, curated by Meg Onli and Alex Da Corte and designed by Irma Boom. It follows Lichtenstein from the 1940s to 1997 outside chronology, pairing paintings with drawings, source material and early work, with circular die cuts through the jacket and pages and two jacket variants.
description.extended:
The catalogue of the Whitney Museum's 2026–27 Lichtenstein retrospective, the first in New York since 1993, designed by Irma Boom with circular die cuts that run from the jacket into the pages.

Meg Onli and the artist Alex Da Corte curated the show and the book. The book covers Lichtenstein from his student years at Ohio State in the 1940s to his death in 1997, sets chronology aside, and pairs finished paintings with preparatory drawings, source materials and rarely seen early work. Texts are by Da Corte, Onli, Dan Nadel, Marshall N. Price and Carmen Winant. Boom cuts a circle through the jacket to the yellow board beneath and repeats the device inside, where openings in the page show the image behind. The jacket was issued in two versions, one with Drowning Girl and one with Little Big Painting. A gatefold reproduces the Greene Street Mural. 366 pages, hardcover, published by the Whitney and distributed by Yale University Press. The exhibition runs 11 October 2026 to 10 May 2027.

Lichtenstein (1923–1997) took his pictures from comic books, advertising and other painters' work and repainted them by hand to look printed. The library holds one of the two die-cut jackets issued. It considers the book's making exemplary: the format, the die cuts throughout, the notebook reproduced on vellum stock, the essay and the layouts.
description.artist_bio: Roy Lichtenstein (1923–1997), New York and Southampton; Pop painter who built his pictures from comic books, advertising and reproductions of other art, painting by hand what looked mechanically printed. First shown in Pop mode at Leo Castelli Gallery in 1962. Estate represented by the Roy Lichtenstein Foundation.
description.exhibition_context: Roy Lichtenstein: Like New, Whitney Museum of American Art, New York, 11 October 2026 – 10 May 2027 (member previews 8–10 October). First New York retrospective since 1993; about 130 works across six decades plus four re-created murals; reunites the works from the 1962 Castelli show. Organized by Meg Onli, Nancy and Fred Poses Curator, and Alex Da Corte, Guest Curator, with Nakai Falcón and David Crane.

notes: Owner's note: the book was issued with two different covers; the library's copy is the die-cut cover. The owner calls it an exceptional publication: everything is right about it, the size, the die cuts throughout, the reproduced notebook printed on vellum, the essay, and the layouts, which are outstanding. Research: the Whitney shop sells two jacket variants, 'Drowning Girl Cover' and 'Little Big Painting Cover', and its product photographs show a circular die cut through BOTH jackets to a yellow board beneath, so 'die-cut' alone does not identify which variant the library holds; confirm with the owner and adjust edition/cover if it is the Little Big Painting jacket. Interior circular die cuts confirmed from the shop's spread photographs (pp. 261, 281); a gatefold for the Greene Street Mural (pp. 247-249) also shown. The vellum notebook reproduction and 'the essay' are the owner's observation only; no source describes them. Contributors beyond Da Corte, Onli, Nadel, Price and Winant: Amazon lists '2 more' unnamed. Dimensions: Yale's page (401 to bots) was unreachable and Amazon's figure (2 x 72.44 x 94.88 in) is corrupt, so height/width left null; measure the copy. Publication date: Rizzoli 13 Oct 2026, Amazon 3 Nov 2026; Whitney shop listed it 7 Oct 2026. Getty SRU has no record yet (0 hits); no LOC/LCSH headings, tags are editorial. Spine credits read 'DA CORTE / ONLI'.
